1. Scope and confirmed findings

Documentation only — no web application changes. Reuse the existing EDUwAI backend and the mobile team's existing stack. No new formatting API, extra model call, provider SDK, dependency upgrade, replacement backend or new database is needed to display an existing answer.

This handoff covers the Student Portal answer body: mathematics, physics notation, chemistry, general-subject Markdown, Indian-language text, typography and narrow-screen containment. It is separate from the earlier input-mode handoff. Source rechecked on 10 October 2026; live production settings, signed-in web UI and the separate mobile repository were not inspected.

Confirmed: both live streaming text and final answer content use AnswerRenderer → StemMarkdownRenderer → react-markdown + remark-math + remark-gfm → rehype-katex/KaTeX, with mhchem enabled. Different subjects do not select different display engines. Fonts, CSS and pre/post-processing are as important as the package names.

Evidence boundary: mobile visibly exposes dollar delimiters and a LaTeX command, whereas web displays mathematical notation. The supplied examples differ in content; there is no verified identical-payload comparison. Missing/bypassed math parsing, escaping, lost backslashes or absent styles are checks for the mobile team, not proven causes.

The rendered fixtures below are produced from the actual unchanged shared component using React server rendering. They are controlled documentation fixtures, not student API responses. They use exported component utilities and KaTeX CSS/fonts; embedded Indic fonts make this document readable offline and are not a new app dependency.

2. Supplied mobile and web answer examples

Account header, account details and unrelated navigation have been excluded. The mobile crop shows some correctly styled bold labels but unparsed mathematical delimiters: Markdown emphasis alone is not enough. Removing dollar signs would hide the symptom while losing equations; the mobile renderer must recognize the math nodes.

Before assigning a root cause, compare the same decoded raw answer string on web and mobile. Check delimiter handling, double-escaping, backslash preservation, the active render path, math plugin/extension activation, KaTeX stylesheet/fonts, available width and any plain-text stripping.

4. End-to-end display pipeline and text ownership

  1. Existing answer API returns Markdown/LaTeX as a Unicode string, not pre-rendered HTML. Decode JSON once and retain the raw answer as canonical state.
  2. During streaming, decode UTF-8 across network chunk boundaries, buffer complete SSE data lines, JSON-parse events and append token content exactly, without inserted spaces or per-chunk trimming.
  3. AnswerRenderer passes content to StemMarkdownRenderer. Empty/whitespace-only content returns no rendered body.
  4. Apply the exact existing preprocessor: convert alternate LaTeX delimiters and bold eligible [Page N] markers. Do not translate the prose, rewrite equations or strip Markdown.
  5. ReactMarkdown runs remark-math and remark-gfm, then rehype-katex with the existing safety/error options. mhchem is already registered.
  6. Custom components style Markdown nodes. KaTeX CSS/fonts produce the equation appearance; answer wrapper and shared CSS contain long expressions.
  7. On completed stream, choose event.answer if truthy, otherwise accumulated tokens. Both completed and streaming text use the same renderer. Preserve raw text separately from the display tree for existing quiz/flashcard/report flows.
Never use stripMarkdown for visual answers. The speech helper removes entire $...$ and $$...$$ segments, code and citations. It is used before speech/explanation, not before StemMarkdownRenderer; reusing it for display can delete mathematical content.

Language resolution in AnswerRenderer influences speech/action props; it does not transliterate, translate, load an Indic SDK or change the Markdown parsing engine. Rendering itself is local and incurs no new answer or voice quota.

5. Exact preprocessing and delimiter rules

Source: src-frontend/components/StemMarkdownRenderer.jsx · lines 9–15

9: function preprocessLatex(content) {
10:   if (!content) return '';
11:   return content
12:     .replace(/\\\[([\s\S]*?)\\\]/g, (_, equation) => `$$${equation}$$`)
13:     .replace(/\\\(([\s\S]*?)\\\)/g, (_, equation) => `$${equation}$`)
14:     .replace(/(?<!\*)\[Page\s*(\d+)\](?!\*)/g, '**[Page $1]**');
15: }
Raw source after JSON decodeExisting handlingImportant boundary
$x^2$remark-math inline node → KaTeX.A literal currency dollar must be escaped in Markdown, e.g. \$50.
$$\nx^2\n$$Multiline display math → block KaTeX.Put delimiters on separate lines when testing display behavior.
\(x^2\)Converted to $x^2$ before Markdown parsing.No whitespace/newline is inserted by preprocessing.
\[x^2\]Converted to $$x^2$$.One-line conversion can still become inline math; $$ alone does not guarantee a block in remark-math.
[Page 12]Regex wraps eligible marker in **...**.Requires exact capital Page + numeric marker; regex has simple neighboring-star guards.

The preprocessor is only three regex replacements. It does not repair every malformed model string, wrap bare commands, add missing braces, detect subjects, normalize all Unicode, insert dollar delimiters or run a conversion API. Because it operates on the whole string before parsing, alternate-delimiter/page-marker changes can also affect text inside code fences; do not describe it as AST-aware.

Sets need escaped braces in LaTeX (\{1,2,3\}), not bare grouping braces. Commands such as \therefore, \frac and \sqrt must be within a math expression to render as mathematical notation. A bare command in prose is not automatically corrected.

6. JSON, Markdown and backslash escaping

There are separate layers: the wire JSON string, the decoded answer string, then Markdown/LaTeX parsing. JSON escaping is not Markdown escaping. Never globally remove or double every backslash after decoding.

Wire JSON (illustrative):
{"answer":"A fraction is $\\frac{1}{2}$. Telugu: తెలుగు."}

After one JSON decode:
A fraction is $\frac{1}{2}$. Telugu: తెలుగు.

Rendered:
Prose + a fraction math node + unchanged Telugu prose.

Native HTTP/JSON libraries normally decode JSON once. A JS source literal also has language-level escaping, so use a raw literal or JSON fixture instead of accidentally turning \\t into a tab or \\f into a control character. Plain \therefore in a decoded string has a literal backslash; an incorrectly authored source/JSON string can lose it before rendering.

Keep UTF-8 decoding state between chunks: a single Indian-script character can span several network byte chunks. Do not parse partial JSON lines, append HTML to a native text label, convert the answer to plain text, or trim each token. The document examples are already decoded strings, not extra JSON-encoded strings.

7. Subject support: one renderer, different content

Subject / contentExisting mechanismWhat the renderer does not do
MathematicsMath nodes with fractions, powers, roots, sets, inequalities, Greek letters, sums and supported KaTeX commands.No symbolic solving, arithmetic correction, diagram plotting or detection/wrapping of unmarked maths.
PhysicsSame math engine; units/vectors expressed explicitly as LaTeX, e.g. \mathrm, \vec, thin spacing.No physics-specific UI package or automatic unit conversion.
Chemistrykatex/contrib/mhchem enables \ce and \pu inside math nodes.Plain H2SO4 in prose is not automatically subscripted. No chemistry model call is part of rendering.
Biology / history / social studiesMarkdown headings, bold/italic, paragraphs, lists, blockquotes and GFM tables.No separate subject formatter, timeline generator or image-conversion pipeline.
Indian languagesUnicode prose through ordinary Markdown; OS/browser font fallback shapes scripts.No translation, transliteration API, language SDK or mandatory Noto download for displaying answers.
Mixed language + notationKeep script text in prose and equations as math nodes; preserve source boundaries.No automatic merging of math font metrics and Indic font shaping; unsupported glyphs inside math \text need testing.

mhchem is a KaTeX extension, not a separate mobile backend/library service. On a different renderer, chemistry support must be verified rather than assumed from basic LaTeX support. Respect KaTeX's supported subset; this is not a full TeX installation with arbitrary macros/packages.

8. Indian-language typography and language resolution

The visible answer body uses the configured CSS system/serif/sans-serif stack. No font is selected per subject or per language in StemMarkdownRenderer. The browser/OS selects available script fonts; KaTeX separately uses its bundled math fonts. Marathi and Hindi share the Devanagari block and cannot be reliably distinguished by a script-only heuristic.

Preserve combining marks, conjunct sequences, line wrapping and mixed English/Indian-script content. Do not transliterate or translate text on display, replace missing characters with Latin approximations, or insert nonbreaking spaces across whole paragraphs. The documentation embeds nine Indic font families only so its offline examples remain readable.

Language-resolution priorityExisting behavior
1: response languageUse responseLang only when it matches a known lowercase key, such as telugu or hindi.
2: user's mediumMap exact known medium names such as Telugu, Hindi or English Medium.
3: source text heuristicCount characters in Indic Unicode blocks; if Indic count / Unicode-letter count <0.2, use english; otherwise choose dominant mapped block.
Fallbackenglish. The heuristic maps Devanagari to hindi, not marathi, unless an earlier priority supplies marathi.

This helper is for speech/action language selection, not the visual font engine. Streaming AnswerRenderer receives content alone, whereas the final renderer receives answer.language if present. The frontend's streamed answerData construction does not copy a language field from done events, so speech may fall back to medium/text detection on that path. Do not invent guaranteed ISO/BCP47 response metadata; known keys map to hi-IN, te-IN, ta-IN, bn-IN, gu-IN, kn-IN, ml-IN, mr-IN, pa-IN, or-IN and en-IN for speech.

The answer wrapper applies fontSize and lineHeight from settings. However the shared paragraph/list classes use leading-relaxed (1.625), which overrides inherited wrapper line-height on those elements. Headings also set their own font sizes/line heights. No new typography endpoint, persisted mobile override or font-family migration is requested. Reuse the existing settings/renderer capabilities on the mobile client where compatible.

Source web flex wrappers are not universally min-width0; the shared content wrapper is. The document examples demonstrate containment without claiming every possible source layout is perfect. Math font baselines/line boxes should be checked on mobile; reducing only prose size or stripping symbols is not parity.

CSS order matters: answer-renderer display-math rules occur after shared renderer rules and override bottom padding while preserving shared top padding. Keep KaTeX's own CSS/font assets; HTML markup alone will look wrong without them.

12. Streaming, completion, fallback and errors

The answer request checks nonblank question and active document before starting. Request/document fences prevent an older query from replacing a newer answer. Raw accumulated tokens are rendered repeatedly through the shared component, so partially received equations can temporarily remain unformatted.

Event / stateExisting behavior relevant to display
tokenAppend event.content exactly; update streamingText; no per-token rendering API.
doneUse event.answer || accumulated;set answer object;clear streaming text;stop streaming. Some cached paths send no answer field and rely on accumulated text.
error eventSet answer to Error: + event.content with empty sources;stop streaming. It is a display/error result, not math repair.
Stream ends without doneIf accumulated is nonempty, promote it as answer with empty sources. No automatic full-answer validation contract.
Transport throws / non-OKExisting client tries the same mode through the non-stream query endpoint; preserve existing billing/auth behavior, not a new formatting retry.
Malformed SSE JSONSource skips malformed data lines. Parser buffers trailing partial line between reads;it is not a generic full SSE implementation.
Incomplete notationlooksUnclosed counts unescaped dollars after removing paired $$ blocks, or finds residual alternate delimiter;adds warning while still rendering processed text.

The actual warning reads “Notation looks incomplete, so the source is shown as typed.” It is heuristic: it does not guarantee every broken $$ block, nested delimiter or unsupported expression is detected, and it does not replace the whole answer with a separate raw-only view. Boundary fallback is a different mechanism.

Do not rewrite an unfinished formula on each chunk, trim whitespace between tokens or permanently store partially rendered HTML. Rendering changing source is expected; the error boundary is keyed by processed text and can reset when new text arrives.

Examples are minimal fixtures, not an exhaustive response schema. mode is the existing answer action (retrieve or explain), never a maths/chemistry rendering flag. top_k is optional in the Phase1 request schema but the shown composer does not send it. No subject, HTML-rendering mode or formatting model field is added here.

Reuse existing Bearer authentication, refresh and organization-context handling where required by the mobile app. Backend document visibility, publication/readiness, authorization and answer-quota checks remain authoritative. HTTP401/403/404/402 and stream error events are not notation failures. Never add a second answer/model request merely because KaTeX could not format a string.

Some backend metadata is source/citation/image/UI context;do not concatenate it into equations. Separate source-page images/diagrams and disclaimer panels from Markdown text. The code-derived API host is https://api.eduwai.in/api; this is not live-health or production-discovery verification. Use the mobile project's approved environment.

14. Safety options and fallback behavior

Setting / mechanismExisting value and consequence
strictfalse;allows supported non-strict constructs,not a guarantee all LaTeX is valid.
throwOnErrorfalse;KaTeX presents errors instead of throwing for ordinary invalid notation.
errorColor#b42318;unknown commands may be red inside normal KaTeX markup;structural parse errors can use katex-error.
trustfalse;do not enable trusted dangerous commands to fix a mobile mismatch.
HTML parsingNo rehype-raw plugin;raw HTML is not executed as answer markup. ReactMarkdown also applies its default URL handling.
RendererBoundaryOn rendering exception,show Some notation could not be formatted. plus original content as React text;keyed by processed content.
Incomplete warningSeparate source heuristic;role=status,12px at default16px;amber-700 #b45309 text.
Fallback styleFlex column,0.35rem gap;3px #d97706 left border;0.7rem left padding;font-size0.9em;source span monospace and pre-wrap.

Keep raw fallback as inert text, not executable HTML. The error boundary catches React render exceptions but does not validate or correct answer facts. This is not a claim that all links, images or arbitrary content have been security-audited; the exact defaults and browser policy must be preserved or assessed by the separate mobile client.

17. Rendered fixtures: ten Indian-language samples

Simple script samples plus an identical math expression exercise Unicode/font shaping and math coexistence. These are font/rendering fixtures, not vetted curriculum translations or per-language backend settings.

18. Mobile adaptation: reuse before adding anything

  1. Identify the mobile project's actual answer display path and compare the same decoded fixture string with web. Do not infer a framework from the screenshot.
  2. Keep the existing HTTP/stream client and EDUwAI services. Feed canonical Markdown/LaTeX text, not a stripped speech string, into the existing mobile answer renderer.
  3. If its current renderer already supports Markdown+math, enable compatible delimiters, chemistry extension, safety options, font assets and containment there. Match the fixtures before choosing any replacement.
  4. If an existing answer WebView renders web content, reuse compatible Markdown/KaTeX support in that established integration, with local/bundled CSS/fonts and restricted unsafe content. This does not mean adding a WebView is mandatory.
  5. For pure native rendering, browser React components are not native widgets. The mobile team must assess its existing parser/math capability; a platform-compatible math layer may be needed if absent. No particular new iOS/Android package, SDK version or architecture is prescribed without that repository.
  6. Apply existing typography, theme, script shaping and scroll rules in the current mobile UI. Keep display math horizontal containment separate from paragraph wrapping;preserve raw answer strings and partial streaming text.
Normal native integration/build work may be necessary in the separate mobile project if it lacks math capability. This handoff requests no web/backend builds, optional feature improvements, provider migrations or mandatory dependency swaps. There is no installed mobile library inventory in this workspace.

The action row in the screenshot is not the math renderer: Read Aloud/Tutor Explanation use separate speech flows;Quiz/Flashcards consume raw content;Report Issue receives context. Do not add them anew or mount the full stateful AnswerRenderer inside a native bridge just to display math. Extract/reuse the content pipeline, and retain already-existing mobile actions.

19. Mobile acceptance and diagnostic checklist

  • Same payload: keep one saved decoded fixture;compare raw text lengths/backslashes/Unicode, not two different model answers. Preserve original content after rendering.
  • Math: set braces, minus/inequalities, powers, fractions, roots, Greek letters, inline baselines, multiline blocks, alternate delimiters and one-line double-dollar limitation.
  • Chemistry/physics: mhchem molecule, ion charge and reaction;explicit units/vectors;plain unmarked formulas remain plain rather than silently invented.
  • Markdown: paragraphs, bold/italic, headings, lists, tables, page markers, blockquote, horizontal rule and current code-node behavior. No unintended stripping of equations.
  • Languages: ten supplied samples;combining/conjunct shaping, English+Indic+math mixture, missing-glyph boxes, accessibility and text-size behavior using existing mobile support.
  • Streaming: token split inside command/brace/dollar and inside UTF-8 character;source persists;partial warning then completed re-render;done without answer uses accumulated text;old query cannot replace new one.
  • Errors/safety: invalid command, malformed braces, incomplete delimiter, inert HTML, unsafe link, trust=false;readable fallback rather than crash, new generation request or content loss.
  • Layout: 320–430px phone widths, landscape, long equation and table scrolling, no whole-page overflow;font/style resources available offline;light/dark current limits acknowledged.
  • API: typography defaults versus saved values;renderer does not consume extra quota;auth/402/stream errors remain distinct from notation failures;no provider credentials on device.

Offline fixture rendering and document checks validate this export. They do not certify the separate mobile implementation, device font availability, live production configuration or the signed-in answer page. Use this checklist when the mobile repository/device tests become available.

65: export default function StemMarkdownRenderer({ content, className = '', compact = false }) {
66:   if (!content?.trim()) return null;
67:   const processed = preprocessLatex(content);
68:   const Wrapper = compact ? 'span' : 'div';
69:   const FallbackWrapper = compact ? 'span' : 'div';
70:   const WarningWrapper = compact ? 'span' : 'p';
71:   const fallback = (
72:     <FallbackWrapper className="stem-renderer-fallback" role="status">
73:       <strong>Some notation could not be formatted.</strong>
74:       <span>{content}</span>
75:     </FallbackWrapper>
76:   );
77: 
78:   return (
79:     <Wrapper className={`stem-markdown-renderer ${compact ? 'stem-markdown-compact' : ''} ${className}`}>
80:       <RendererBoundary key={processed} fallback={fallback}>
81:         <ReactMarkdown
82:           remarkPlugins={[remarkMath, remarkGfm]}
83:           rehypePlugins={[[rehypeKatex, {
84:             strict: false,
85:             throwOnError: false,
86:             errorColor: '#b42318',
87:             trust: false,
88:           }]]}
89:           components={compact ? compactComponents : baseComponents}
90:         >
91:           {processed}
92:         </ReactMarkdown>
93:       </RendererBoundary>
94:       {looksUnclosed(processed) && (
95:         <WarningWrapper className="stem-renderer-warning" role="status">
96:           Notation looks incomplete, so the source is shown as typed.
97:         </WarningWrapper>
98:       )}
99:     </Wrapper>
100:   );
101: }
102:

12:   english: 'en-IN',
13: };
14: 
15: const MEDIUM_TO_LANG = {
16:   'Hindi': 'hindi',
17:   'Telugu': 'telugu',
18:   'Tamil': 'tamil',
19:   'Bengali': 'bengali',
20:   'Gujarati': 'gujarati',
21:   'Kannada': 'kannada',
22:   'Malayalam': 'malayalam',
23:   'Marathi': 'marathi',
24:   'Punjabi': 'punjabi',
25:   'Odia': 'odia',
26:   'English': 'english',
27:   'English Medium': 'english',
28: };
29: 
30: const SCRIPT_LANG_MAP = [
31:   { range: [0x0900, 0x097F], lang: 'hindi' },
32:   { range: [0x0980, 0x09FF], lang: 'bengali' },
33:   { range: [0x0A00, 0x0A7F], lang: 'punjabi' },
34:   { range: [0x0A80, 0x0AFF], lang: 'gujarati' },
35:   { range: [0x0B00, 0x0B7F], lang: 'odia' },
36:   { range: [0x0B80, 0x0BFF], lang: 'tamil' },
37:   { range: [0x0C00, 0x0C7F], lang: 'telugu' },
38:   { range: [0x0C80, 0x0CFF], lang: 'kannada' },
39:   { range: [0x0D00, 0x0D7F], lang: 'malayalam' },
40: ];
41: 
42: export function detectLanguageFromText(text) {
43:   if (!text) return 'english';
44:   const counts = {};
45:   let letterTotal = 0;
46:   for (const ch of text) {
47:     const code = ch.codePointAt(0);
48:     if (/\p{L}/u.test(ch)) letterTotal++;
49:     for (const { range, lang } of SCRIPT_LANG_MAP) {
50:       if (code >= range[0] && code <= range[1]) {
51:         counts[lang] = (counts[lang] || 0) + 1;
52:         break;
53:       }
54:     }
55:   }
56:   if (!letterTotal) return 'english';
57:   const indianTotal = Object.values(counts).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
58:   if (indianTotal / letterTotal < 0.2) return 'english';
59:   return Object.entries(counts).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])[0][0];
60: }
61: 
62: export function resolveLanguage(responseLang, userMediumName, answerText) {
63:   if (responseLang && LANGUAGE_TO_BCP47[responseLang]) {
64:     return responseLang;
65:   }
66:   if (userMediumName) {
67:     const fromMedium = MEDIUM_TO_LANG[userMediumName];
68:     if (fromMedium) return fromMedium;
69:   }
70:   if (answerText) {
71:     return detectLanguageFromText(answerText);
72:   }
73:   return 'english';
74: }
75: 
76: export function isIndianLanguage(langCode) {
77:   return (
78:     langCode !== 'english' &&
79:     !!LANGUAGE_TO_BCP47[langCode] &&
80:     LANGUAGE_TO_BCP47[langCode] !== 'en-IN'
81:   );
82: }
83: 
84: export function toBcp47(langCode) {
85:   return LANGUAGE_TO_BCP47[langCode] || 'en-IN';
86: }
87: 
88: export function stripMarkdown(text) {
89:   if (!text) return '';
90:   return text
91:     .replace(/\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g, '$1')
92:     .replace(/\*([^*]+)\*/g, '$1')
93:     .replace(/`{1,3}[^`]*`{1,3}/g, '')
94:     .replace(/#{1,6}\s/g, '')
95:     .replace(/\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)/g, '$1')
96:     .replace(/!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]+\)/g, '')
97:     .replace(/^\s*[-*+]\s/gm, '')
98:     .replace(/^\s*\d+\.\s/gm, '')
99:     .replace(/\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$/g, '')
100:     .replace(/\$[^$]+\$/g, '')
101:     .replace(/\[Page\s*\d+\]/g, '')
102:     .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
103:     .trim();
104: }
